t: The kingdom grew from the union of the Svear around Uppsala and the Geats of the south-west around the year 1000.
Under Gustav II Adolf and his successors it became the dominant Baltic power, winning German lands at Westphalia in 1648.
Defeat at Poltava in 1709 ended its empire; after 1814 it kept out of war and built a model welfare state.
dyk: The Riksbank, founded in 1668, is the oldest central bank still in operation, and its predecessor Stockholms Banco issued Europe’s first banknotes in 1661.
ev: Uppsala becomes the seat of an archbishopric
Sweden joins Denmark and Norway in the Kalmar Union
Gustav Vasa is elected king and Sweden leaves the Kalmar Union
Gustav II Adolf is killed at the Battle of Lützen
The Peace of Westphalia gives Sweden lands in northern Germany
Charles XII is defeated by Peter the Great at Poltava
Finland is ceded to Russia by the Treaty of Fredrikshamn

f.capital: Uppsala region (itinerant medieval kings); Stockholm from the later Middle Ages
f.founder: Eric the Victorious and Olof Skötkonung
